title: bug: scaffold missing @stackwright/collections and lucide-react deps
description:
## What breaks

A freshly-scaffolded project (via `npx launch-stackwright`) fails `next build` immediately with two module-not-found errors:

```
./app/_components/providers.tsx:6:1
Module not found: Can't resolve '@stackwright/collections'

./stackwright-generated/icons.ts:6:1
Module not found: Can't resolve 'lucide-react'
```

## Where it breaks

1. `providers.tsx` imports `FileCollectionProvider` from `@stackwright/collections`, but that package is not injected into the scaffolded project's `package.json` by the scaffold generator.
2. The generated `stackwright-generated/icons.ts` (produced by `stackwright-prebuild`) imports from `lucide-react`, but `lucide-react` is also absent from the scaffolded project's `package.json`.

Both are runtime/build-time hard dependencies that every scaffolded project needs; neither is optional.

## Fix location

The scaffold template generator — most likely `packages/launch-stackwright/src/index.ts` or the scaffold template files it uses — needs to inject both of the following as dependencies in the generated `package.json`:
- `@stackwright/collections`
- `lucide-react`

## Evidence

`scaffold-smoke-test` CI check failing on `dev` branch across 3+ consecutive runs. See PR #467 for CI logs.

title: checkForPlaintextSecret: add high-entropy detection for real tokens (bi-directional check)
description:
The checkForPlaintextSecret function in packages/types/src/types/secret-detection.ts currently warns when entropy is low (< 3.8) — catching human-readable plaintext passwords stored in integration auth YAML fields.

However, there are two distinct threat classes that one threshold can't catch:
- Low entropy (< 3.8): human-readable passwords like "password123"
- High entropy (> 4.5): real cryptographic tokens like JWTs, bearer tokens, API keys stored directly in YAML

The current check only catches the first class. A JWT stored as `token: "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiJ9..."` passes through silently.

Suggested fix: change the condition to `entropy < 3.8 || entropy > 4.5` to catch both classes. Update the warning message to distinguish which case triggered.

Additional context: checkForPlaintextSecret is currently exported but never called (dead code). This issue should also cover wiring it into the prebuild pipeline at the integration auth processing point in packages/build-scripts/src/prebuild.ts. Consider adding a minimum length guard (e.g., skip values < 32 chars for the high-entropy check) to reduce false positives from short but random-looking strings.

title: perf/benchmarks: fix performance budget files and reset to meaningful targets post-optimization
description:
## Goal
Fix the current state where performance budgets are meaningless ('current + 10% headroom') and the comments in `bundle-size.bench.ts` are badly out of sync with `performance-budgets.json`. Set real forward-looking targets once optimization work lands.

## Current problems
1. `performance-budgets.json` first-load JS budget: 450KB max. Benchmark comments in `bundle-size.bench.ts` say baseline was ~85KB and budget was <100KB. Nobody updated the comments when the budget was bumped.
2. Benchmarks have been failing for ~1 month — the budget ceiling has likely been breached even at 450KB as new features shipped.
3. The `performance.yml` CI workflow is the actual gate; any mismatch between it and `performance-budgets.json` creates confusion about what the real enforcement is.

## Tasks
- [ ] Sync the comments in `bundle-size.bench.ts` with `performance-budgets.json` (do this now, independent of optimization)
- [ ] After optimization work lands (icons + code-splitting beads), set new meaningful targets in `performance-budgets.json`
- [ ] Proposed targets post-optimization: first-load JS warn 150KB / max 200KB, all-pages JS warn 600KB / max 800KB
- [ ] Consider adding `@next/bundle-analyzer` output as a CI artifact on every PR for visibility (not a gate, just a report)
- [ ] Update the benchmark README comments and PERFORMANCE.md to reflect the new architecture

## Can be done in two phases
- **Phase 1 (now)**: Fix the comment/budget mismatch — pure maintenance, no optimization needed
- **Phase 2 (after optimization)**: Set the new meaningful budget numbers

## Dependencies
- Phase 2 depends on icons bead (stackwright-zkq) and code-split bead (stackwright-mp6) landing first
close_reason: Phase 1 (comment sync) and Phase 2 (new meaningful targets) both done. ADR written at docs/adr/bundle-architecture.md. first-load budget: 150KB warn / 200KB max.

title: perf/code-split: implement dynamic import pattern for optional heavy content types
description:
## Goal
Establish and implement a code-splitting pattern for content types that are heavy but not universally used (carousel, video, potentially others identified by the audit).

## Background
All content types registered via `DefaultStackwrightComponents` and `@stackwright/core` exports are currently loaded synchronously. For sites that don't use a carousel or video, they still pay the JS cost for those components.

The map content type has already solved this problem with a registry/provider pattern — it has zero weight in the base bundle unless the provider is explicitly registered. That pattern is a good model.

## Tasks
- [ ] Define the dynamic import pattern to use (Next.js `dynamic()` wrapper, React.lazy + Suspense, or registry async-loader) — decision from RFC bead
- [ ] Identify which content types are candidates for code-splitting based on bundle audit
- [ ] Implement the pattern for the top 2–3 candidates first (likely: carousel, video)
- [ ] Add to AGENTS.md: 'When adding a new content type with >20KB gzipped weight, use [pattern]'
- [ ] Measure before/after first-load JS impact

## Dependencies
- RFC bead (stackwright-y5u) must resolve the code-splitting pattern choice
- Audit bead (stackwright-9yh) confirms which content types are worth splitting
close_reason: Dynamic imports implemented for Carousel and fuse.js/SearchModal. React.lazy() in componentRegistry + tsup splitting:true creates real ESM chunks. Carousel removed from main barrel, available at @stackwright/core/carousel. fuse.js dynamic import in SearchModal useEffect. Suspense boundary added in DynamicPage. No API changes. All 503 tests pass.

title: perf/icons: implement prebuild icon manifest — generate per-site static lucide imports
description:
## Goal
Replace lucideAllIconsPreset with a prebuild-generated per-site icon manifest that contains ONLY the icons actually used in the site's YAML content. Eliminates ~120KB gzip from first-load JS.

## Approach
The stackwright-prebuild script (in @stackwright/build-scripts) will:
1. After processing all YAML content to JSON, recursively walk all page data
2. Collect all { type: 'icon', src: string } objects across all pages
3. Resolve legacy MUI aliases (hard-coded map, candidates for future deprecation)
4. Write public/stackwright-content/_icon-manifest.json (debug artifact)
5. Write stackwright-generated/icons.ts with static lucide imports + registerSiteIcons() function

## Generated file shape
```typescript
// GENERATED by stackwright-prebuild — do not edit. Run pnpm predev to regenerate.
import { Star, Moon, Sun } from 'lucide-react';
import { registerStackwrightIcons } from '@stackwright/icons';
import { BlueSkyIcon } from '@stackwright/icons/icons/social/BlueSkyIcon';
import { StackwrightIcon } from '@stackwright/icons/icons/brand/StackwrightIcon';

export function registerSiteIcons(): void {
  registerStackwrightIcons({ Star, Moon, Sun, bluesky: BlueSkyIcon, stackwright: StackwrightIcon });
}
```

## Wiring
- No webpack alias needed — generated file is in user app directory, Next.js webpack processes it natively and tree-shakes lucide-react
- defaultIcons.ts fallback: swap lucideAllIconsPreset → lucideIconPreset (curated subset, ~43 icons)
- launch-stackwright templates: Providers.tsx calls registerSiteIcons() from generated file
- stackwright-generated/ added to .gitignore

## Tasks
- [ ] Add collectIconSrcs() recursive walker to prebuild.ts
- [ ] Add LEGACY_MUI_ICON_ALIASES hard-coded map and SYSTEM_ICON_NAMES set to prebuild.ts
- [ ] Add generateIconManifest() function to prebuild.ts
- [ ] Call generateIconManifest() in main prebuild flow after all pages processed
- [ ] Update defaultIcons.ts: swap lucideAllIconsPreset → lucideIconPreset
- [ ] Update launch-stackwright templates (Providers.tsx pattern)
- [ ] Add stackwright-generated/ to .gitignore
- [ ] Document in AGENTS.md
- [ ] Build + measure before/after on docs example; document savings

## Notes
- lucideAllIconsPreset and registerAllLucideIcons() are KEPT as opt-in exports for power users
- System icons (Sun, Moon, Info, AlertTriangle, CircleAlert) always included regardless of YAML content
- Legacy MUI aliases are hard-coded in prebuild scanner (option B) and are candidates for deprecation
close_reason: Prebuild icon manifest implemented. collectIconSrcs + generateIconManifest added to prebuild.ts. defaultIcons.ts now uses curated preset as fallback. Scaffold template updated to registerSiteIcons(). AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md updated.

title: perf/rfc: define first-load bundle contract and code-splitting standards for the framework
description:
## Goal
Have the architectural discussion and document a clear standard: what belongs in the base first-load bundle vs. what should be a dynamically-imported chunk or separate package.

## Background
The framework has accumulated heavy dependencies without a stated policy on bundle boundaries. The current approach treats everything in `@stackwright/core` and `@stackwright/icons` as first-load, regardless of whether a given site uses those features.

Key tension: the icon registry pattern (`registerDefaultIcons()` at app startup) is fundamentally incompatible with tree-shaking. A site using 5 icons loads 1,300.

A curated icon preset (`lucideIconPreset` in `packages/icons/src/presets/lucideIcons.ts`) already exists but is not the default.

## Questions to resolve in this RFC
1. **Icon loading strategy**: Should `registerDefaultIcons()` switch to the curated `lucideIconPreset` (subset), or should we move to a different pattern entirely (e.g., explicit per-icon registration, or lazy icon loading)?
2. **Content type chunking**: Should heavy content types (carousel, video) be dynamically imported rather than in the synchronous `@stackwright/core` bundle? If yes, what's the pattern — Next.js `dynamic()`, React `lazy()`, or a registry-level async loader?
3. **First-load contract**: What is the *explicit list* of what must be in first-load JS? Proposal: React + Next.js runtime, theme/color system, app bar/nav, DynamicPage shell. Everything else is a candidate for code splitting.
4. **New dependency policy**: What gate should new heavy dependencies (>20KB gzipped) pass before being added to an eagerly-loaded package? Proposal: requires explicit ADR noting bundle impact and code-splitting strategy.
5. **Benchmark target**: Once optimized, what should the first-load JS budget be? Proposal: 150KB warn / 200KB max (includes React + Next.js ~80KB + framework shell ~70-120KB).

## Deliverables
- [ ] Discussion captured in this bead's comments
- [ ] Decision recorded as a `bd remember` for each resolved question
- [ ] ADR doc added at `docs/adr/bundle-architecture.md`
- [ ] Updated target budgets documented (feeds the benchmarks bead)

## Dependencies
Audit bead (stackwright-9yh) should be done first for real numbers.
notes: RFC RESOLVED 2026-05-29. All 5 decisions locked based on stackwright-9yh audit data (392KB→~227KB gzip target, 42% reduction). Decision 1: Prebuild icon manifest (generateIconManifest in build-scripts, outputs stackwright-generated/icons.ts with static lucide imports). Decision 2: next/dynamic for carousel/video/SearchModal. Decision 3: First-load contract documented in ADR. Decision 4: >20KB gzip dep requires ADR. Decision 5: 150KB warn/200KB max post-optimization. Implementation: zkq (icon manifest), mp6 (content split), pez (budget reset), new ADR doc.
close_reason: RFC complete. All 5 architectural decisions recorded. Implementation tracked in zkq, mp6, pez.

title: perf/audit: bundle composition audit — identify exact contributors to 400KB+ first-load JS
description:
## Goal
Get a definitive, reproducible breakdown of what is inside the first-load JS bundle so we can make informed decisions about what to optimize.

## Background
The first-load JS bundle has grown from ~85KB (Jan 2025 baseline) to ~403KB+ — a 5× increase. The current performance budget in `performance-budgets.json` was bumped to 450KB to match current size rather than as a meaningful target. Benchmarks have been failing for ~1 month.

Key finding from prior analysis: the map component is **not** in the base bundle (it uses a registry/provider pattern). The most likely primary contributor is the icon system — `registerDefaultIcons()` uses `lucideAllIconsPreset` which imports `{ icons }` from `lucide-react`, pulling in all ~1,300 Lucide icons eagerly.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add `@next/bundle-analyzer` to `examples/stackwright-docs` dev dependencies
- [ ] Run a production build with `ANALYZE=true pnpm build` and screenshot/export the bundle treemap
- [ ] Document the top 10 contributors to first-load JS by size (gzipped)
- [ ] Confirm or deny: is `lucide-react` the largest single contributor?
- [ ] Check if `js-yaml`, `zod`, or other server-only packages are leaking into the client bundle
- [ ] Document findings as a comment on this bead before closing

## Success Criteria
A ranked list of bundle contributors with sizes that can feed the RFC bead (stackwright-XXX).

## Blocks
RFC bead for bundle architecture decisions.

comments.author: Stackwright Bot
comments.text:
## Bundle Audit Findings — 2025-05-29

### Methodology
- Added `@next/bundle-analyzer` to `examples/stackwright-docs`
- Ran `ANALYZE=true npx next build --webpack` (Turbopack doesn't support analyzer)
- Parsed the embedded JSON data from the HTML treemap reports
- Aggregated module sizes by package

### Total First-Load JS

| Chunk | Raw | Gzipped |
|---|---|---|
| webpack runtime | 1.7 KB | 0.9 KB |
| framework (React) | 185 KB | 58 KB |
| main (Next.js) | 134 KB | 38 KB |
| polyfills | 110 KB | 38 KB |
| **_app (Stackwright)** | **918 KB** | **255 KB** |
| page chunk | ~0.3 KB | ~0.2 KB |
| **TOTAL** | **1,349 KB** | **392 KB** |

### Top 10 Contributors Inside _app (918KB parsed / 255KB gzipped)

| # | Package | Parsed | Gzip | % of _app | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **lucide-react** | 471 KB | 123 KB | **51.3%** | ALL 1,500+ icons via `{ icons }` barrel import |
| 2 | @stackwright/core | 106 KB | 33 KB | 11.6% | Monolithic barrel export, includes all components |
| 3 | next (internals) | 97 KB | 35 KB | 10.6% | otel, buffer, _document, image, link |
| 4 | **zod** | 95 KB | 24 KB | **10.4%** | **LEAKED** to client via @stackwright/types |
| 5 | **js-yaml** | 31 KB | 10 KB | **3.4%** | **LEAKED** to client via @stackwright/themes/themeLoader |
| 6 | tailwind-merge | 29 KB | 7 KB | 3.2% | Required by @stackwright/ui-shadcn |
| 7 | fuse.js | 19 KB | 6 KB | 2.1% | SearchModal — arguably client-side, but could be lazy |
| 8 | @stackwright/types | 18 KB | 5 KB | 2.0% | Type schemas (zod-based) leaking to client |
| 9 | @opentelemetry/api | 12 KB | 4 KB | 1.4% | Next.js internal dependency |
| 10 | Radix UI (combined) | 16 KB | 5 KB | 1.8% | Accordion, Tabs, Collection, etc. |

### Key Findings

**1. ✅ CONFIRMED: lucide-react is the #1 contributor at 51.3%**
- Root cause: `registerDefaultIcons()` calls `lucideAllIconsPreset` which does `import { icons } from 'lucide-react'` — this imports ALL 1,500+ icons
- A curated preset (`lucideIconPreset`) already exists with ~40 icons that would tree-shake properly
- **Estimated savings: ~450 KB parsed / ~120 KB gzip** by switching to curated preset

**2. ⚠️ zod IS leaking to client (95 KB + 18 KB = 113 KB)**
- Import chain: `_app → @stackwright/core → @stackwright/types → zod`
- `@stackwright/types` uses zod for schema definitions — these are build/CLI concerns, not runtime client needs
- **Estimated savings: ~113 KB parsed / ~29 KB gzip** if types/schemas are server-only

**3. ⚠️ js-yaml IS leaking to client (31 KB)**
- Import chain: `_app → @stackwright/core → @stackwright/themes → themeLoader.ts → js-yaml`
- ThemeLoader parses YAML at runtime to load embedded themes — but by the time the client runs, themes should already be JSON from prebuild
- **Estimated savings: ~31 KB parsed / ~10 KB gzip**

**4. fuse.js is client-side (19 KB) — acceptable but improvable**
- Used by SearchModal for client-side fuzzy search — this IS a client feature
- However, it could be dynamically imported (`next/dynamic`) to not block first load
- **Potential savings: ~19 KB from first-load** (still loaded on search open)

**5. @stackwright/core at 106 KB is concerning**
- Single barrel export bundles ALL components (DynamicPage, PageLayout, SearchModal, Carousel, etc.)
- No code splitting — every component is in the first-load regardless of page content
- This should be split into entry points or use dynamic imports for heavy components

### Summary: Theoretical Maximum Savings

| Fix | Parsed savings | Gzip savings |
|---|---|---|
| Switch to curated icon preset | ~450 KB | ~120 KB |
| Keep zod/types server-only | ~113 KB | ~29 KB |
| Keep js-yaml server-only | ~31 KB | ~10 KB |
| Lazy-load fuse.js/SearchModal | ~19 KB | ~6 KB |
| **Total potential** | **~613 KB** | **~165 KB** |

This would bring first-load JS from ~392 KB gzip down to ~227 KB gzip — a 42% reduction.

### Analyzer HTML Reports
Saved at `examples/stackwright-docs/.next/analyze/{client,nodejs,edge}.html`

title: refactor(cli): replace gh CLI in git open-pr with generic git push
description:
The `stackwright git open-pr` command in packages/cli/src/commands/git-ops.ts uses the `gh` CLI for two things: (1) `gh pr create` to open a pull request, and (2) the shared `gh()` utility in utils/git.ts. This creates a hard dependency on GitHub and the gh CLI for what is fundamentally a content publishing workflow.

Proposed replacement:
- Replace `gh pr create` with a plain `git push` followed by a printed URL hint or provider-detected PR link (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea all support opening PRs from a push URL)
- Remove the `gh()` utility from utils/git.ts once it has no remaining callers
- Update the `stackwright_open_pr` MCP tool description accordingly

This unblocks citizen developers using Gitea, Codeberg, GitLab, or any other git host.
